title: The Spirit of Masonry
author: William Hutchinson
epithet: The first attempt to give the Craft a philosophy
summary: Hutchinson's lectures, the earliest book to read Masonic ritual as a coherent moral and religious system rather than a set of customs — the beginning of the 'philosophical' interpretation of the Craft.

title: The Freemason's Monitor
author: Thomas Smith Webb
epithet: The book that shaped the American ritual
summary: Webb's monitor, which fixed the form of the American 'Preston-Webb' ritual and lectures for the whole nineteenth century — the working handbook behind most United States lodges.

title: The True Masonic Chart, or Hieroglyphic Monitor
author: Jeremy Ladd Cross
query: True Masonic Chart Hieroglyphic Monitor Cross
epithet: The engraved emblems every American lodge knew
summary: Cross's illustrated monitor, whose engravings of the Masonic emblems — the broken column, the weeping virgin, the beehive — became the standard iconography of the American Craft.

title: The Antiquities of Freemasonry
author: George Oliver
epithet: The Craft traced back to the patriarchs
summary: Oliver's attempt to root Freemasonry in a pure primitive religion running from Adam and the patriarchs — the high tide of the mythical, antiquarian school of Masonic history he did most to build.
imprint: London: G. and W. B. Whittaker, 1823

title: The Historical Landmarks and Other Evidences of Freemasonry Explained
author: George Oliver
epithet: Two volumes of the old symbolic lore
summary: Oliver's two-volume compendium of Masonic symbolism, legend and lecture — the fullest statement of the learned, credulous tradition that later 'authentic' historians spent decades correcting.

title: The Symbolism of Freemasonry
author: Albert G. Mackey
epithet: The science of Masonic symbols, systematised
summary: Mackey's systematic reading of the Craft's symbols and legends as a coherent 'science of symbolism' — for a century the standard American statement of what the emblems are held to mean.

title: A Lexicon of Freemasonry
author: Albert G. Mackey
epithet: The dictionary that preceded his encyclopaedia
summary: Mackey's early dictionary of Masonic terms, offices and symbols — the reference that made his name and grew, over thirty years, into the great Encyclopaedia.

title: The Royal Masonic Cyclopaedia
author: Kenneth R. H. Mackenzie
epithet: The occultist's dictionary of the higher degrees
summary: Mackenzie's cyclopaedia, steeped in the fringe rites and Rosicrucian lore of the SRIA — a reference whose entries fed directly into the founding of the Golden Dawn.

title: The Origin of the English Rite of Freemasonry
author: William James Hughan
query: Origin of the English Rite of Freemasonry Hughan
epithet: The documentary turn in Masonic history
summary: Hughan's evidence-based reconstruction of how the English craft degrees actually took shape — a founding work of the 'authentic school' that replaced Oliver's legends with records.

title: History of Freemasonry
author: Joseph Gabriel Findel
epithet: The German critical history, Englished
summary: Findel's history, the first to apply German documentary rigour to the Craft's origins and to reject the fanciful genealogies — a landmark of continental Masonic scholarship in English translation.

title: General History, Cyclopedia and Dictionary of Freemasonry
author: Robert Macoy
query: Cyclopedia and Dictionary of Freemasonry Macoy
epithet: The publisher-Mason's illustrated reference
summary: Macoy's popular illustrated cyclopaedia, which put a compact history and dictionary of the Craft — with plates of regalia and emblems — on the shelf of nearly every American lodge.

title: The Poetry of Freemasonry
author: Rob Morris
epithet: The poet laureate of the Craft
summary: The collected Masonic verse of Rob Morris, crowned 'poet laureate of Freemasonry' — sentimental, ubiquitous, and a window on how the nineteenth-century lodge imagined itself.

title: Freemasonry and the Ancient Gods
author: J. S. M. Ward
query: Freemasonry and the Ancient Gods Ward
epithet: The Craft as a survival of the mysteries
summary: Ward's argument that Masonic ritual preserves the initiations of the ancient mystery religions — the fullest statement of the mystical, anthropological reading that flourished between the wars.

title: An Interpretation of Our Masonic Symbols
author: J. S. M. Ward
query: Interpretation of Our Masonic Symbols Ward
epithet: Every emblem read as a mystery-teaching
summary: Ward's handbook decoding the Craft's symbols one by one as fragments of an ancient initiatory science — a staple of the between-the-wars esoteric lodge.

title: The Secret Tradition in Freemasonry
author: A. E. Waite
epithet: Waite's mystical genealogy of the degrees
summary: Waite's two volumes tracing a hidden mystical tradition through the Craft and high degrees — learned, sceptical of the wilder claims, and the mature statement of his esoteric Masonry.

title: The Masonic Initiation
author: W. L. Wilmshurst
epithet: The lodge as a school of the soul
summary: Wilmshurst's sequel to The Meaning of Masonry, reading the degrees as a graded discipline of inner initiation — the most influential mystical interpretation of the Craft in English.

title: The Secret Societies of All Ages and Countries
author: Charles William Heckethorn
query: Secret Societies of All Ages and Countries Heckethorn
epithet: A gazetteer of the world's hidden orders
summary: Heckethorn's two-volume survey of secret societies from the ancient mysteries to the Carbonari — the Victorian encyclopaedia of the subject, and a quarry for every later conspiracy writer.

title: An Exposition of the Mysteries
author: John Fellows
query: Exposition of the Mysteries Fellows Masonry
epithet: The Craft explained by the ancient rites
summary: Fellows's derivation of Masonic ceremonies from the mysteries of Egypt, Greece and the Druids — an early and much-read attempt to explain the ritual by comparative religion.

title: Duncan's Masonic Ritual and Monitor
author: Malcolm C. Duncan
epithet: The famous printed guide to the three degrees
summary: Duncan's illustrated exposition of the ritual of the first three degrees and beyond, with its diagrams of the floor and the signs — the best-known 'exposure' of the working, still in print.

title: Light on Masonry
author: David Bernard
epithet: The great anti-Masonic exposé of the Morgan affair
summary: Bernard's collection of ritual exposures, published at the height of the Anti-Masonic excitement that followed the disappearance of William Morgan — a hostile witness that preserved much of the working.

title: The Arcana of Freemasonry
author: Albert Churchward
epithet: The signs of the Craft traced to prehistoric man
summary: Churchward's diffusionist reading of Masonic signs and symbols as survivals from a single prehistoric religion born in Africa — the eccentric fringe of Edwardian Masonic anthropology.

title: Notes on the Scientific and Religious Mysteries of Antiquity
author: John Yarker
query: Notes Scientific Religious Mysteries of Antiquity Yarker
epithet: The high grades traced to the ancient mysteries
summary: Yarker's survey of the mysteries of antiquity and the 'high grade' Masonic and Rosicrucian systems descended from them — the learning behind his own fringe rites of Memphis and Misraim.

title: Traditions of Freemasonry and Its Coincidences with the Ancient Mysteries
author: A. T. C. Pierson
epithet: The Craft set beside the old initiations
summary: Pierson's account of Masonic tradition and its parallels with the ancient mystery-religions — one of the mid-century American works that framed the Craft as heir to the initiations of antiquity.

title: A General History of Freemasonry in Europe
author: Emmanuel Rebold
query: General History of Freemasonry in Europe Rebold
epithet: The Craft's spread across the Continent
summary: Rebold's history of European Freemasonry, tracing the orders and their political entanglements across France, Germany and beyond — a standard continental survey Englished for American readers.

title: The Travels of Cyrus
author: Chevalier Andrew Michael Ramsay
epithet: The philosophical romance of the Oration's author
summary: Ramsay's hugely popular didactic romance on the education of a prince in the ancient mysteries — by the Jacobite whose 'Oration' gave Freemasonry its chivalric origin-legend.

title: Illustrations of Masonry (Oliver edition)
author: William Preston
query: Illustrations of Masonry Preston Oliver notes
epithet: The lectures that formed the English ritual
summary: Preston's Illustrations, the book that codified the English lectures and the 'Prestonian' system of the degrees — here in the enlarged edition with George Oliver's notes.

title: General Ahiman Rezon and Freemason's Guide
author: Daniel Sickels
query: General Ahiman Rezon and Freemason's Guide Sickels
epithet: A monitor and guide for the American lodge
summary: Sickels's widely used monitor, gathering the lectures, charges and ceremonies of the American Craft under the old title 'Ahiman Rezon' — a working manual with engraved emblems.

title: Washington and His Masonic Compeers
author: Sidney Hayden
query: Washington and His Masonic Compeers Hayden
epithet: The founding fathers gathered in the lodge
summary: Hayden's account of George Washington and the Revolutionary generation as Freemasons — the book that fixed the patriotic American image of the Craft as a school of republican virtue.

title: Signs and Symbols Illustrated and Explained
author: George Oliver
query: Signs and Symbols Illustrated Explained Oliver
epithet: A course of lectures on the first degree
summary: Oliver's lectures on the signs and symbols of the first degree, expounded through his sweeping comparative mythology — the symbolic school of Masonic teaching at its most characteristic.

title: The Book of the Chapter
author: Albert G. Mackey
query: Book of the Chapter Mackey Royal Arch
epithet: A monitor of the Royal Arch degrees
summary: Mackey's monitor of the capitular or Royal Arch degrees, setting out their ceremonies and symbolism — his guide to the system of Masonry beyond the three Craft degrees.

title: Book of the Words
author: Albert Pike
query: Book of the Words Pike Scottish Rite
epithet: Pike on the sacred words of the Rite
summary: Pike's study of the significant words of the Scottish Rite degrees and their supposed roots in the ancient languages — a companion to Morals and Dogma from the Rite's great systematiser.

title: A Concise History of Freemasonry
author: Robert Freke Gould
epithet: The authentic historian in one volume
summary: Gould's single-volume distillation of his monumental history — the mature 'authentic school' account of the Craft's origins and spread, cautious with legend and grounded in the records.

title: Freemasonry Before the Existence of Grand Lodges
author: Lionel Vibert
query: Freemasonry Before the Existence of Grand Lodges Vibert
epithet: The Craft in the century before 1717
summary: Vibert's careful account of the lodges and manuscripts of the seventeenth century, before the Grand Lodge era — a key work of the documentary school on Masonry's obscure beginnings.

title: The Origin of Masonic Ritual
author: F. de P. Castells
epithet: The ritual traced to its Hebrew and Kabbalistic roots
summary: Castells's argument that the Craft ritual and its words descend from Hebrew and Kabbalistic sources — a scholarly-fringe study typical of the esoteric wing of early-twentieth-century Masonry.

title: Things a Freemason Should Know
author: Frederick J. W. Crowe
query: Things a Freemason Should Know Crowe
epithet: A pocket handbook of Craft knowledge
summary: Crowe's compact guide to the history, symbolism and practice a Mason was expected to know — one of the small self-improvement handbooks that furnished the Edwardian lodge library.

title: The Book of the Lodge
author: George Oliver
epithet: How to furnish and govern a lodge
summary: Oliver's practical manual on the constitution, furniture and government of a lodge, with its symbolism — the working companion to his many volumes on Masonic antiquity.

title: The New Book of Constitutions (1738)
author: James Anderson
epithet: Anderson's enlarged second Constitutions
summary: The revised and enlarged 1738 edition of Anderson's Constitutions, which rewrote the mythical history and set down the laws of the Grand Lodge — the founding charter-book in its expanded form.
imprint: London: for Brothers Caesar Ward and Richard Chandler, 1738

title: The Revelations of a Square
author: George Oliver
query: The Revelations of a Square Oliver
epithet: A genial history of the lodge through its worthies
summary: Oliver's affectionate, anecdotal history of English Freemasonry told through the 'revelations' of an old tracing-board — a lively picture of lodge life and its great characters in the eighteenth century.

title: A Manual of the Lodge
author: Albert G. Mackey
query: A Manual of the Lodge Mackey
epithet: The monitorial instruction of the three degrees
summary: Mackey's monitor of the ceremonies and lectures of the symbolic lodge, with the meaning of its emblems — one of the most widely used American guides to the working of the three degrees.

title: The Religion of Masonry
author: Joseph Fort Newton
epithet: The faith implicit in the Craft
summary: Newton's reflective account of the religious spirit he saw at the heart of Freemasonry — tolerant, symbolic and undogmatic — by the minister-Mason whose 'The Builders' was already a standard.

title: Emblematic Freemasonry
author: A. E. Waite
epithet: Waite on the symbols and the secret tradition
summary: Waite's essays on the emblematic and mystical side of the Craft — the secret tradition he believed the symbols concealed — a companion to his larger Secret Tradition in Freemasonry.

title: Military Lodges: The Apron and the Sword
author: Robert Freke Gould
query: Military Lodges Apron and Sword Gould
epithet: Freemasonry in the marching regiments
summary: Gould's history of the travelling military lodges that carried Freemasonry across the British Empire with the army — a distinctive chapter of the Craft's spread, by its foremost historian.

title: Woman and Freemasonry
author: Dudley Wright
epithet: The women admitted to the lodge and its rites
summary: Wright's history of women's relation to Freemasonry — the female initiates, the adoptive rites and the mixed orders — a pioneering survey of a subject the regular Craft mostly ignored.
